entries.label: M-02
entries.title: NAV-anchored minOut is execution-price-blind, enabling sandwich value leak
amplifiedBy: M-04 (run-07 — amplification under non-zero aggregate buffer)
entries.reconfirmedNote: Reconfirmed OPEN at reflax-yield-vault-07 (5f9abdd). story-042 did not change the minOut derivation: minOut is still NAV-anchored on both fast and buffered paths. New finding M-04 (ryv7m4) demonstrates the M-02 leak is AMPLIFIED by 1/(1-f) on the buffered path when the aggregate buffer fraction f > 0; the bound the M-02 acceptance memo relied on (slippageBps * tradeSize against recipient principal) is parametrically breached under non-zero buffer. Author acknowledgement remains authoritative for the f=0 case; M-04 carries the upgraded mitigation surface.
entries.triageNote: Accepted by design (route: sUSDe/USDe). The strategy anchors swap minOut to ERC4626 NAV (convertToShares/convertToAssets) rather than an oracle or signed price, a deliberate trust-minimization choice. Review confirmed there is no oracle-free, single-transaction way to detect a skewed pool — the obvious get_dy execution-time cross-check is circular (it reads the reserves an attacker would have just skewed) — so the alternatives (oracle distortion, signer compromise) trade a bounded, quantifiable leak for unbounded trust assumptions. We accept the residual. Residual risk (retained, bounded): up to slippageToleranceBps × tradeSize per swap; economically marginal on the deep sUSDe/USDe pair at normal trade-size-to-depth, growing with looser tolerance, thinner pools, depeg windows, or large swaps relative to depth; bounded because sUSDe NAV is not atomically manipulable (cannot escalate to theft on this route). Compensating control to carry upstream: slippageToleranceBps has no upper bound and defaults to 0 — add a require-enforced hard ceiling + sane nonzero default; operationally keep tolerance near organic slippage and consider private orderflow for large rebalances. Forward-looking: do not deploy this strategy over an ERC4626 whose share price is atomically manipulable — there the NAV reference becomes attacker-controlled and the same code path is a High-severity theft primitive. The merged ex-M-03 last-withdrawer amplification does not apply: clients are owner-curated (setClient onlyOwner), not mutually-distrusting; the requested-not-received decrement is documented-intentional protocol-owned yield. Triaged 2026-05-27.

entries.story: story-042 — per-client setAsideBuffer added to skimSurplus
entries.borderlineNote: Medium vs High judgment call; promotion triggers documented in finding record.
entries.note: Dispute upheld (review-finding ryv7m4). Core claim is false: report asserts the recipient absorbs the ENTIRE trade slippage over a (1-f) principal => effectiveBps = slippageBps/(1-f). But _distributeBuffer computes buf = underlyingReceived * bufferShares[i]/totalShares off the ACTUAL post-swap proceeds, so clients get f*underlyingReceived and recipient gets (1-f)*underlyingReceived — both scaled by the same (1-s). Slippage is shared strictly proportionally; the recipient's loss vs its own entitlement is exactly slippageBps for all f. The PoC's '200bps' is a denominator artifact: it divides the WHOLE trade's leak (recipient slice + clients slice) by ONLY the recipient principal, and never asserts on actual recipientReceived. PoC's own logs at f=50%: entitlement 0.0200, received 0.0198 = 100bps loss, not 200. Counter-test workspace/reflax-yield-vault/test/poc-M04-REFUTATION.t.sol measures recipient real effective bps flat at ~100 across f={0,25,50,75}% (finding predicted 100/133/200/400), all PASS. The only real adjacent issue (no aggregate buffer cap -> recipient take can reach 0) is already filed as L-03. Marked false-positive 2026-05-28.

The crediting itself is documented intended design (DEDUP-001 suppressed; severity-classifier Low, severity-auditor REFUTED), but it materially widens the blast radius of THIS Low: the deposit-side haircut magnitude is bounded ONLY by the still-missing slippageToleranceBps upper cap, so an owner setting a loose tolerance now haircuts depositors' credited principal as well as swap minOut. entries.label: H-02
entries.title: _totalWithdraw ignores the Phase-1 cached amount and re-reads live clientBalances, allowing inter-phase deposits to be silently extracted and causing underflow that bricks the two-phase withdrawal mechanism
entries.suppressionReason: Manual review (run-11): invalid as High. Over-extraction is circular/owner-funded; underflow unreachable because clientBalances[client] <= totalDeposited holds by construction (deposit/withdraw move both by the same delta). The Halmos underflow proof was a spurious symbolic artifact treating the two as independent free symbols. Only residual is the misleading WithdrawalExecuted event, already tracked as L-06. Future sanitizer runs should suppress re-flagging. See reports/reflax-yield-vault-11/submissions/rejected/REJECTION-RATIONALE.md.

entries.suppressionReason: Manual review (run-11): owner already holds totalWithdrawal + emergencyWithdraw escape hatches to the same funds, so the 24h timelock is cosmetic by design in an owner-trusted model.
